rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation of eligible-row filtering only; i2441 (2025) p.3 Line2/Column(d) reports expenses for a listed qualifying person. The reply chooses the supplied gross expense amount for an eligible row and zero otherwise; the project filters at form aggregation. This does not certify the reply eligibility predicates or alter the existing amb.2025.dc_line30 gross-column/net-line30 choice. No new owner approval or per-person benefit allocation is claimed.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error with the prior presentation ambiguity retained; i2441 (2025) pp.3-4 Column(d) excludes benefits for the person listed, but the reply subtracts the entire form-level line28 from every dependent entry. A household total is not a per-person allocation: with two people each having $1,000 expenses and $1,000 total excluded benefits, applying that same subtraction to both rows removes $2,000. The current interface supplies gross entry expenses and adjusts benefits once at form level. The existing gross-column/net-line30 choice amb.2025.dc_line30 remains recorded; this ruling makes no new owner decision or claim of per-row allocation support.

Its inlined dependent.claimed now puts sibling_descendant with household_member and other under the all-year, local-law route (12 months and dependent.lawful), the reading of finding L1, which the project now shares (L1 fixed; executed: /tmp/adj-s19r3/w_sibdesc_false.json gives claimed no, w_sibdesc_true.json claimed yes); last round's model error (sibling_descendant as a listed relative) is gone. It also asks dependent.lawful of household_member, whose answer already states the condition ("if your relationship did not violate local law", dependent.relationship): an extra question with no amount. No. STOP You can't claim this child as a dependent". Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.deepseek.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 6,036 agree; 293 value (130 completed), 134 project-refuses, 125 project-unknown, 76 candidate-refuses (47 completed), 110 candidate-unknown. The reply validates and runs. Its errors: (1) household_member counts with any months (classm.dependent.4.deepseek dep_a, 10 months; project no, candidate yes), against the all-year bullet; sibling_descendant (a grandniece, not a listed relative) likewise counts without the all-year test; (2) the qualifying-child route omits Step 2's citizenship test (classm.f8995a.2 and classm.qdcg.2 dep_b, a child aged 3, citizen no; project no, candidate yes); (3) the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records withholding multiple_support): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply". Records with married no and joint_return yes (classm.dependent.3.deepseek and classm.dependent.5.deepseek dep_b, classm.sc.1 dep_b; project yes, candidate no) contradict the married question itself ("Was this person married at the end of 2025 ..., or is this person filing a joint return for 2025"), whose yes is refused (i1040gi p. 21, Married person); a consistent answer gives both sides the same result: representation. The project-refuses are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited screen of i1040gi p. 22 ("You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)"; classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.2), and dependent.income_exception (pp. 19-20, Exception to gross income test; classm.sc.1), all on returns the full interview refuses: scope. The project-unknown are partial records withholding an answer the interview asks of every listed person (tin, months, citizen, married, other_claimant, divorced_rule are read before any relationship branch) and older fixtures: no tax quantity differs. The candidate, like the project, counts other with 12 months without the local-law condition (finding F2, raised on the Claude log). Project stands on this log's differences.

The project supplies Count1 and filters at f2441.qp_count; the second supplies Count1 conditionally. This adjudicates only placement of the count filter, not correctness of the second qualifying-person predicate, whose defects are ruled separately. The candidate's disabled route is "dc_incapable and months > 6", with no death-year rule, though dependent.born_died and dependent.part_year_home were published (BUG-0157 added dependent.dc_lived_half after round 2, so round 2's scope ruling no longer covers the line): p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "In determining whether a person is a qualifying person, a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". Witness by reading (not executed): regression stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (BUG-0157): a disabled parent, age 80, who died in 2025, months 0 as the months question instructs for a non-qualifying-child person not with you the entire time, born_died yes, part_year_home yes, dc_incapable yes, dc_paid $4,000; the project gives dc_qp yes (dependent.dc_lived_half), 2(d) $4,000 and f2441 line 11 $600; the candidate's disabled route needs months > 6 and gives dc_qp no. Other differences: (a) its route for a disabled person who would be a dependent except for gross income or a joint return is behind the project's cited screen f2441.nondependent (i2441 p. 1, "or could claim as a dependent except"), scope; (b) it omits f2441.care, which reaches no amount (Form 2441 sums only where dc_qp holds and is not completed without care); (c) sa.dependent omission is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead); (d) its sibling_descendant variant is the odc_person error.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error in the child alternative; i2441 (2025) p.1 requires a qualifying child under13, not every claimed dependent under13. The corrected reply tests claimed, residence and age but does not require qualifying-child status, so an unrelated all-year QR child can be treated as a care qualifying person without incapacity. Its separate QR category omissions can also reject eligible disabled relatives. The reply contains valid age-boundary structure, but no contract cases are executed because dc_count fails types.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope/representation on admitted dependent-care facts; i2441 (2025) p.1 supplies the under13 and disabled-person alternatives. The reply now derives the age regimes without requiring an unnecessary dc_under13 answer and matches all ten declared qualifying-person outputs. It additionally encodes disabled would-be dependents that this project refuses through f2441.nondependent; no admission or equivalence of that excluded regime is claimed. The missing care-screen factor is irrelevant on the active care rows compared here. Its separate column(c) contract failure remains blocking.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; numeric count literals in the returned h_lived_half (6) and the household-year test (12) omit type:Count. Untyped numbers are money cents in the declared IR, so comparing them with Count months yields unknown; the typed project comparison yields a Boolean. This affects the transitive dependency of this line. The raw response is preserved, not silently repaired. BUG-0129 records that the comparer erases the annotation; .transcription/constant-unit-erasure-witness.json confirms the false-agreement mechanism. This is a model IR error, not a project tax-value finding. The separate transcription qualification hold remains in force.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: "collection parent binding mismatch", a sum over the dependent collection inside a dependent entry), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. i1040gi p. 41, Step 3: a qualifying child for the EIC meets the relationship, age and joint return tests and "lived with you in the United States for more than half of 2025"; p. 44, Married child and Qualifying child of more than one person. The reply's test is the project's: the age test is written as (under 19, or a full-time student under 24) and younger than you, or disabled, which distributes to the project's (under qc.age_limit and younger) or (under qc.student_age_limit, a student and younger) or disabled, with the constants 19 and 24 equal to those parameters; the open status is the structural comparison of the two forms. Its other_claimant and married refusals are the project's; it also refuses divorced_rule, which the project computes (the EIC follows the child's residence, and a child of divorced parents who did not live with you for more than half the year fails us_half): an over-refusal. The project-refuses are claimed_no_tin (cited), the project-unknown partial records withholding tin. Project stands.

As last round the reply requires 7 or more months of everyone and has no part-year route (born_died, placed, part_year_home were published), so a parent who died after living with the filer for more than half of the part of the year she was alive (stage8.hoh.parent.died_lived_part_year, stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year) and the child placed during the year (stage8.hoh.adopted_part_year) do not qualify the filer, by reading (project yes on those completed fixtures). Its exclusion of a dependent only through the member-of-household route (sibling_descendant, household_member, other) and its route for an unmarried qualifying child who is not your dependent are the project's; its divorced_rule, married, other_claimant and multiple_support refusals are refusals in the project too (scope on those).

The project-unknown are records without the part-year answers that the interview asks for a relative with 6 months or fewer (classm.f8962.4.deepseek dep_b, classm.asset.3): the candidate does not ask them because it lacks the rule. (1) The candidate requires months > 6 for every Test 2 person, with no part-year route for a relative other than a qualifying child born, dying, adopted or placed in 2025, though dependent.born_died, dependent.placed and dependent.part_year_home were published: i1040gi p. 15: "If the person is your qualifying child, the child must have lived with you for more than half the part of the year the child was alive. If the person is anyone else, see Pub. 501. Similarly, if you adopted the person ... the person is considered to have lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your main home was this person's main home for more than half the time since the person was adopted or placed with you in 2025"; p501 p. 9, Death or birth: "Your qualifying child or qualifying relative who lived with you for more than half the part of the year they were alive". Witness by reading (not executed): regression stage8.hoh.adopted_part_year (BUG-0158): an adult child adopted in 2025, a qualifying relative with months 0 and part_year_home yes, placed yes; the project gives hoh_test2 yes (line 12e $23,625 head of household), the candidate gives no because it needs months > 6; the stage8 death-year parent case (born_died yes, part_year_home yes) is the same. (2) Its dependent test counts a sibling_descendant qualifying relative who did not live with you all year: i1040gi p. 19, Step 4: a qualifying relative is your "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" or "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household" (a grandniece or a stepsibling's child, the project's sibling_descendant, is not in the relationship list); such a person is not your dependent, so Test 2 (i1040gi p. 14, item 1(b)) cannot use them. Round 2 ruled the same two errors. sa.dependent omission is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 and Step5 require the all-year household route for otherwise eligible other/sibling_descendant relationships and identification for both filers when jointly filing. The corrected reply QR helper excludes those relationships outright and its ODC predicate omits household.all_tin. An eligible all-year distant relative can be wrongly rejected, and the filer-TIN prerequisite is not encoded. Invalid dc_count is a separate form-level failure, not a reason to treat these source omissions as equivalence.

The reply omits the ODC citizenship and household.all_tin tests, and its QR relationship helper omits sibling_descendant even when the person meets the all-year household condition. The published enum reserves that category for more distant relatives; a lawful all-year eligible person may qualify under Step4. These are source/interface omissions, not equivalence or new owner scope choices.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; f1040s8812 line 7, "Multiply line 6 by $500"; inherited from odc_person (same 2,552 records). i1040gi p. 19, Step 5 (the credit for other dependents for a dependent who is not a Step 3 child). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the returned h_qr_relationship treats sibling_descendant as an unconditional listed Step4 relative and omits other even with twelve household months. The published input defines sibling_descendant as more distant descendants (for example grandnieces and a stepsibling child); listed nieces/nephews are already in sibling. i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 requires the all-year household condition for these other relationships; p501 p.19 excludes foster parents from listed parents. On the saved seven-month distant-relative case the project gives ODC false/$0, the actual model gives true/$500; an all-year other household member reverses that error. The actual-expression witness is .transcription/dependent-age-claude-witness.json. Untyped Count constants are an additional model IR defect (BUG-0129), not an excuse to call the trees equivalent.

As last round the reply has no filer identification test (household.all_tin was published), so a dependent of a filer with neither an SSN nor an ITIN gets $500. Its claimed, TIN, citizenship and not-a-child-tax-credit-child tests are the project's. Its inlined dependent.claimed now puts sibling_descendant with household_member and other under the all-year, local-law route (12 months and dependent.lawful), the reading of finding L1, which the project now shares (L1 fixed; executed: /tmp/adj-s19r3/w_sibdesc_false.json gives claimed no, w_sibdesc_true.json claimed yes); last round's model error (sibling_descendant as a listed relative) is gone.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on admitted eligible-TIN facts; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Steps4-5 requires the same QR income/support/residency/all-year relationship conditions and ODC citizenship/household identification conditions. The reply places dependent.tin inside claimed instead of as a separate ODC factor; both are true on admitted identified dependents. Its MFJ/claimable-filer branch extends a refused regime, and lack-of-dependent-TIN refusal placement differs; neither excluded regime is admitted by this ruling. The separate HOH and care-box defects remain pending.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 and Step5 require the all-year household route for otherwise eligible other/sibling_descendant relationships and identification for both filers when jointly filing. The corrected reply QR helper excludes those relationships outright and its ODC predicate omits household.all_tin. An eligible all-year distant relative can be wrongly rejected, and the filer-TIN prerequisite is not encoded. Invalid dc_count is a separate form-level failure, not a reason to treat these source omissions as equivalence.

The reply omits the ODC citizenship and household.all_tin tests, and its QR relationship helper omits sibling_descendant even when the person meets the all-year household condition. The published enum reserves that category for more distant relatives; a lawful all-year eligible person may qualify under Step4. These are source/interface omissions, not equivalence or new owner scope choices.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 19, Step 5 (the credit for other dependents for a dependent who is not a Step 3 child). Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.deepseek.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 4,222 agree; 2,126 value (1,099 completed), 183 candidate-unknown, 76 candidate-refuses, 134 project-refuses, 33 project-unknown. The test is the project's, but it excludes the candidate's ctc_child, which wrongly includes qualifying relatives under 17, so those relatives lose the $500 credit (the ctc_child witnesses, mirrored), and its dependent.claimed adds the errors ruled there (household_member and sibling_descendant without the all-year test, no citizenship test on the child route; the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records withholding multiple_support): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply"). The project-refuses are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited screen of i1040gi p. 22 ("You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)"; classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.2), and dependent.income_exception (pp. 19-20, Exception to gross income test; classm.sc.1), all on returns the full interview refuses: scope. The project-unknown are partial records withholding an answer the interview asks of every listed person (tin, months, citizen, married, other_claimant, divorced_rule are read before any relationship branch) and older fixtures: no tax quantity differs. Project stands.

(1) The candidate omits the filer SSN-or-ITIN test (household.all_tin: every person has a TIN or applied for an ITIN): i1040gi p. 19, Step 5: "1. Did you, and your spouse if filing a joint return, have either an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)? ... No. STOP You can't claim the credit for other dependents"; p. 17, Before you begin: "If you want to claim the credit for other dependents, you, and your spouse if filing jointly, must have either an SSN or ITIN"; a filer with no SSN or ITIN gets $500 per other dependent where the source gives none. (2) Its qualifying-relative route treats sibling_descendant as a relative who need not live with you all year: i1040gi p. 19, Step 4: a qualifying relative is your "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" or "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household" (a grandniece or a stepsibling's child, the project's sibling_descendant, is not in the relationship list). (3) Omitting sa.dependent (listed as a refusal gate) is scope: the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead. (4) Its added "dependent.joint_return is no" on the qualifying-relative route is representation, because dependent.qualifying_relative refuses on dependent.married (i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, question 3, "See Married person").

These are invalid returned IR, preserved without repair or execution. This adjudicates the invalid-IR objection only; source/representation differences still require a valid replacement review. It establishes no project tax defect or numeric assertion, and the run remains pending under BUG-0129.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the returned h_qr_relationship treats sibling_descendant as an unconditional listed Step4 relative and omits other even with twelve household months. The published input defines sibling_descendant as more distant descendants (for example grandnieces and a stepsibling child); listed nieces/nephews are already in sibling. i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 requires the all-year household condition for these other relationships; p501 p.19 excludes foster parents from listed parents. On the saved seven-month distant-relative case the project gives ODC false/$0, the actual model gives true/$500; an all-year other household member reverses that error. The actual-expression witness is .transcription/dependent-age-claude-witness.json. Untyped Count constants are an additional model IR defect (BUG-0129), not an excuse to call the trees equivalent.
